Class: counts from tomorrow, not from today
Caption: 33 nights. It starts tomorrow.
Why: The caption counts the nights of the run, which begin the day after the post. 09/29 to 10/31 inclusive is 33, so the trailer is right on 09/28. C04 counts from the post's own day and reads 34. The missing data is a column saying what day a countdown counts from.

Class: UTC day is not the audience day
Caption: Samhain is 5 nights out.
Why: Scheduled 00:30 UTC on 10/27, which is 19:30 Central on 10/26. The audience sees it on 10/26, when Samhain is 5 nights out, so the caption is true. C04 reads the UTC date. Anything placed between 00:00 and 05:00 UTC publishes the previous evening locally and reads as drifted when it is not. The missing data is the campaign's timezone.

Class: a story is not a feed post
Caption: Full reel on my page.
Why: C05 exists because 2 reels published seconds apart split the audience and took 1818 views to 162. A story does not compete in the feed. Counting the 20:15 story against the 18:30 reel turns 9 real collisions into 25, and a gate that cries wolf 16 times out of 25 is a gate somebody switches off. The missing data is the surface a post lands on.

Caption: 2 Instagram reels, 18:00 and 18:30
Why: 30 minutes apart on 1 account. The worst of the 9 that survive the story split. Not fixed, because fixing it moves a live post.

Class: no concept of a rolling load horizon
Caption: n/a
Why: The 33 night run is loaded into Blotato by .github/workflows/halloween-33.yml, which books 7 days ahead and runs daily at 12:00 UTC. It succeeded on 09/23, 09/24 and 09/25. A night past that 7 day window is not a broken promise, it is a night the loader has not reached yet, and on 09/26 C13 reported 28 dark nights on Instagram for exactly that reason. The missing data is the campaign's load horizon: how many days ahead the queue is expected to be filled. Beyond it C13 should stay quiet; inside it a dark night is still real and still the finding. Without the column the rule cries wolf every night, which is how a rule gets switched off. The other half of the same gap: if the loader fails for 7 days straight the run goes dark and nothing here would say so, because the gate cannot tell a night the loader will fill from a night it never will.
